title: Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026: Rare Earths
date_evidence: U.S. Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries, February 2026
key_claim: In April 2025 China tightened rare-earth export controls (samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium, yttrium), expanded them in October (europium, holmium, erbium, thulium, ytterbium) and in November suspended the October controls for one year; magnets were the leading global end use; substitutes are available for many applications but generally are less effective.
verbatim_quote: Substitutes are available for many applications but generally are less effective.
notes: Structural anchor - Tier 1 primary commodity data; the substitution-efficacy line anchors the counter-argument.

title: Global EV Outlook 2026: Electric vehicle batteries
date_evidence: the IEA Global EV Outlook 2026 was published in May 2026 ... LFP accounted for over half of EV batteries and over 90% of battery energy storage systems globally
key_claim: Battery chemistry is shifting toward cheaper LFP, which now accounts for over half of EV batteries and over 90% of stationary battery storage globally, while interest in sodium-ion is growing and being scaled by CATL and BYD for small-range cars, urban light commercial vehicles, two- and three-wheelers and stationary storage.
notes: Tier 1 IEA flagship; quantifies demand-side chemistry substitution away from nickel/cobalt.

title: Global implications of export controls on rare earths: a model-based assessment (Occasional Paper Series No. 384)
date_evidence: European Central Bank (ECB) paper ... was published on March 31, 2026 ... models a hypothetical 18-month stringent export ban ... 0.3-0.6% output loss in the U.S. and Euro area ... permanent technological substitution
key_claim: An ECB model of an 18-month stringent rare-earth export ban projects a 0.3-0.6% output loss in the US and euro area with inflationary pressure, and warns of long-term self-inflicted damage to China through accelerated global supply-chain diversification and permanent technological substitution.
notes: Tier 2 central-bank research; names permanent technological substitution as a structural consequence of export controls.

publisher: Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS)
title: Rare Earth Export Restrictions One Year Later
key_claim: One year after China's 2025 rare-earth export restrictions exposed a critical US national-security vulnerability, Washington responded with billions of dollars in financing and global partnerships, but the United States remains far from true supply-chain resilience.
notes: Tier 2 think-tank; frames the supply-side response and its resilience gap (the consensus the signal sits beneath).

title: China's rare-earth dominance keeps EV makers dependent
date_evidence: published on March 17, 2026 by Rest of World ... Tesla ... next-generation motors expected in 2026 will again be rare earth-free
key_claim: Western automakers including Stellantis, General Motors and Honda are funding rare-earth-free motor alternatives such as Niron Magnetics' iron-nitrogen magnets, and Tesla's next-generation 2026 motors are slated to be rare-earth-free, but China's cost advantage remains hard to crack and building independent supply chains could take 15 years.
notes: Tier 3 journalism; supplies OEM substitution momentum and the strongest counter-evidence (cost advantage hard to escape).

title: The energy transition has a rare earth problem: these startups are solving it
date_evidence: climatechangenews.com/2026/05/05/the-energy-transition-has-a-rare-earth-problem-these-startups-are-solving-it ... startups building a new generation of motors made without rare earths
key_claim: A wave of companies including Advanced Electric Machines and Niron Magnetics is commercialising rare-earth-free motors and magnets built from abundant materials such as electrical-steel laminations and iron-nitrogen, with several targeting market entry around 2026-2027.
notes: Tier 3 journalism; corroborates the substitution build-out across motor technologies.

title: Grid-forming, hybrids and alternative chemistries in Wood Mackenzie's 2026 energy storage trend predictions
key_claim: Alternative battery chemistries are emerging at scale: sodium-ion offers compatibility with existing lithium-ion manufacturing lines and is beginning to scale internationally, with Wood Mackenzie pointing to the largest planned sodium-ion project to date in the US.
notes: Tier 2 consultancy analysis via trade press; sodium-ion scaling as a demand-side substitution vector for nickel/cobalt/lithium.
